summary.headline: Anup Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue rose 46% QoQ to INR182 crores, but EBITDA margin was 9.6%; FY27 guidance is INR840-860 crores revenue.
summary.overview: Q2 consolidated revenue was INR182 crores, up 46% from Q1, with EBITDA of INR17.5 crores (9.6%) as fixed-cost under-absorption (fixed cost INR62 crores) and about 6% elevated material cost plus about 2% inward freight weighed on margins. Management attributed weak H1 to low order booking in H1 FY26 (about INR250 crores versus a normal INR500-600 crores requirement), which left thin-margin orders executing in H1 FY27. FY27 guidance is revenue of INR840-860 crores and EBITDA of INR120-128 crores (14-15% margin), implying a 20-22% margin in Q4 on newer, better-priced orders. Order intake and the pending order book improved: pending order book is INR941 crores as of date, and new order intake for FY27 is INR674 crores as of date.

segments.name: Product mix (by product)
segments.commentary: Heat exchangers about 51% of revenue, vessels and reactors about 42%, silos and other components about 7%.

segments.name: End-market mix
segments.commentary: About 80% of revenue from oil and gas, petrochemicals and thermal power; Middle East about 30% of annual revenue, with Saudi Aramco and ADNOC as the two focus customers.

segments.name: Anup Technical Services
segments.commentary: Three sites under execution, completion planned in H2 FY27; FY27 revenue expected around INR50 crores at 30-40% margin; target INR200 crores in three years.

segments.name: Mabel (Chennai)
segments.commentary: Acquired for southern footprint and silos/tanks capability; FY27 revenue expected INR65-70 crores versus about INR43 crores in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR840-860 crores and EBITDA of INR120-128 crores (about 14-15% margin), contingent on executing to plan.
Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin needed at about 20-22% to hit the guided EBITDA range; management said Q4 projects are priced at 20%+ margins.
Target order intake of INR250-300 crores per quarter going forward, given about 11-12 month order-to-delivery cycle.
Expect to open FY28 (1 April 2027) with pending order book of INR800-900 crores; FY28 revenue growth guided at about 20%.
Around INR400 crores of pending order book carried into next financial year, covering about 5 months of FY28 revenue.
Export share expected to return to about 50% of revenue next year; US target about 30% of exports; Nigeria and Kenya as African growth regions.
No major capacity capex for at least two years; Mabel has no planned capex for two years; Kheda bay covering to be completed by December 2026.
capex_capacity: Capacity across Ahmedabad, Kheda and Chennai is about 20,000 metric tons per year, convertible to about INR1,200 crores revenue at a good product mix.
Kheda bay covering (bay number one) is the last capacity expansion, to be wound up by December 2026.
Management expects no further capacity capex for at least two years; incremental capex only for capability.

Acquisitions to be for capability (technology), not capacity, over the next 2-3 years; exploring a technology deal (e.g., AI data-centre cooling, close to heat exchangers) and possible Middle East manufacturing.
demand_pricing: New order intake FY27 YTD INR674 crores as of date; pending order book INR941 crores as of date.
Added proprietary licensed products in H1: two from Lummus Technology (Netherlands), one each from TKIS (Germany) and L&T; two more global licences expected to be qualified this year.
Proprietary products carry about INR8-10 crores per equipment versus about INR3 crores average today; fewer competitors (two or three globally).
Management says new orders are at much improved margins because bids now use current elevated raw material costs; royalties are built into cost and apply to all competitors.
Historical inquiry-to-order conversion 15-20%; management targets about 25% going forward.
Tier 1 Indian competitors named: L&T, Godrej, ISGEC.
Demand outlook: thermal power strong for at least 3 years in India; fertiliser projects picking up in India, Africa and South America; nuclear cited as a future opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are the exact order intake and order book numbers for the quarter ended September?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book as of 30 Sep 2026 was INR864 crores (INR941 crores as of date); FY27 YTD intake was INR597 crores as of 30 Sep (INR674 crores as of date).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is Letter of Intent (LOI)?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40 crores of the order book is LOI; work has started on these and formal POs typically follow in 2-3 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What order intake run rate is expected from Q4 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was about INR310 crores and Q2 about INR283 crores; management intends to book INR250-300 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 margin improvement arithmetic consistent with guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: Q4 needs about 20-22% EBITDA margin to reach INR120-128 crores; management said Q4 execution is priced at 20%+ margins, with the full-year average at 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Middle East exposure driving H1 weakness, and how will geographic mix diversify?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are FOB India port so the Q1 impact was not due to Middle East exposure; Middle East is about 30% of annual revenue and is a growth focus, with US (target about 30% of exports), Nigeria and Kenya as expansion regions.

qa_highlights.question: Will licensed-product orders have lower margins given royalties?
qa_highlights.answer: Royalties are built into cost and apply equally to all bidders; management declined to commit to a 20% EBITDA margin, saying percentage margins will be lower but absolute EBITDA per tonne will be higher.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the H1 margin squeeze and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY27 executed orders were booked in H1 FY26 at aggressive margins to cover fixed costs; order scarcity was a bigger driver than raw material and geopolitical impacts, and newer orders are priced on current costs.

qa_highlights.question: Are technical services included in the INR1,200 crore capacity figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; technical services currently use existing plant resources and are part of the INR1,200 crore capacity.

risks_watch: Q4 FY27 must deliver about 20-22% EBITDA margin to meet the guided INR120-128 crore EBITDA; Q2 margin was 9.6%.
Shipping costs (more than double, per management) and raw material prices remain volatile; procurement windows are 2-3 weeks.
Revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4 must land as planned; H1 FY27 revenue was low because of thin H1 FY26 order intake.
Export mix of about 50% depends on overseas order flow; current export backlog is about 33-34%.
Two more global licence qualifications expected within this year; proprietary product execution and royalty costs to be tracked.
Order intake needs to stay at INR250-300 crores per quarter to hold the INR800-900 crore opening order book for FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the H2 ramp and order book, but candid that H1 was disappointing; management was more cautious on the margin recovery, saying historic margins are still challenging and that shipping remains uncertain.
key_quotes: The revenue numbers for H1 are in line with our plan, and new projects are moving well on the shop floor, with good revenue milestones landing in quarter three and quarter four.
I don't think we have ever had above INR900 crores pending order book.
Mohit, the order scarcity and starvation in the first half of last year is a bigger contributor to the to the challenging performance than the raw ma terial and geopolitical impacts.

adds.what: Kheda bay covering (bay number one), last capacity expansion, to be wound up by December 2026

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR840-860 crores (about 5-10% growth, midpoint ~7.5%) and EBITDA INR120-128 crores, backed by pending order book of INR941 crores and FY27 intake of INR674 crores, though Q4 needs a 20-22% margin and no specific capacity is being added for two years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 9.6%, and guidance of INR120-128 crores needs about 20-22% in Q4 on newer orders priced at 20%+ margins, against a 14-15% full-year average.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kheda bay covering is the last expansion, due by December 2026, and management expects no further capacity capex for at least two years, with capacity at about 20,000 MT per year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR840-860 crores (about 5-10% growth), backed by a pending order book of INR941 crores and FY27 intake of INR674 crores, with H2 ramp expected.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capacity utilisation was not disclosed, and management said no capacity capex for at least two years, with only capability-led spend and possible technology acquisitions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is new and conditional on Q4 margins of 20-22%, and Q2 margin of 9.6% gives no evidence of running ahead.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin was 9.6% against the 20-22% Q4 needed, and shipping costs have more than doubled with raw material prices still volatile.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two more global licence qualifications are expected this year after two Lummus and one each from TKIS and L&T were added in H1, with proprietary products at INR8-10 crores per equipment versus about INR3 crores average.

rows.label: Order intake target INR250-300 crores per quarter
rows.why: Q1 intake was about INR310 crores and Q2 about INR283 crores, and FY27 YTD intake is INR674 crores, which supports the INR800-900 crore FY28 opening order book.

rows.label: Export share back to about 50% and US/Africa push
rows.why: Exports were about 50% of revenue in H1 and are expected to return to about 50% next year, but the current export backlog is only about 33-34%.

rows.label: Anup Technical Services scale-up to INR200 crores in three years
rows.why: Three sites are under execution with completion planned in H2 FY27 and FY27 revenue of about INR50 crores at 30-40% margin, but the INR200 crore target is three years out.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 ramp, order book (INR941 crores) and proprietary licences, but cautious on margin recovery, shipping costs and the H1 order shortfall; analysts pushed on the 20-22% Q4 margin needed.
